stem: A reusable flexible bronchoscope has just been used for a client. Which reprocessing step is required before the bronchoscope is used again?

options.A: Meticulously clean the bronchoscope, including accessible internal channels, and then perform at least high-level disinfection before reuse.
options.B: Use low-level surface disinfection only if the previous client had no known infection.
options.C: Perform high-level disinfection without prior cleaning as long as the disinfectant is circulated through the bronchoscope.
options.D: Reprocess only the exterior surface because the bronchoscope's internal channels do not require the same level of cleaning.

rationale: Current CDC disinfection guidance states that heat-sensitive flexible endoscopes, including bronchoscopes, must be properly cleaned and at minimum undergo high-level disinfection after each use. CDC further states that meticulous cleaning must precede high-level disinfection or sterilization and that endoscope reprocessing includes cleaning both external surfaces and internal channels before high-level disinfection. Therefore A is correct. B provides an inadequate level of reprocessing, C incorrectly omits the essential cleaning step, and D ignores the internal channels that must also be cleaned and disinfected.
educational_objective: Reprocess a reusable flexible bronchoscope by meticulous cleaning of external surfaces and internal channels followed by at least high-level disinfection before the device is reused.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Disinfection of Healthcare Equipment — Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities
source_version_date: CDC web guidance November 28, 2023, based on CDC Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities; live currentness rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Flexible endoscopes/bronchoscopes section: all heat-sensitive endoscopes including bronchoscopes must be properly cleaned and at minimum high-level disinfected after each use. Cleaning section: meticulous cleaning must precede high-level disinfection or sterilization. Reprocessing steps include cleaning external surfaces and brushing/flushing internal channels before high-level disinfection with perfusion of accessible channels.
source_claim_supported: Reusable flexible bronchoscopes require meticulous cleaning, including internal-channel cleaning, followed by at least high-level disinfection after each use before reuse.

source_original.stem: A reusable flexible bronchoscope has just been used for a client. Which reprocessing step is required before the bronchoscope is used again?

options.A: Meticulous cleaning followed by at least high-level disinfection is required before a reusable flexible bronchoscope is used again.
options.B: Low-level surface disinfection is adequate when the bronchoscope was used in a client without a known infection.
options.C: High-level disinfection can be performed effectively without prior cleaning of the bronchoscope channels.
options.D: Reprocessing the exterior surface is sufficient because internal channels do not contact mucous membranes.

source_original.rationale: CDC classifies heat-sensitive flexible endoscopes such as bronchoscopes as devices that must be properly cleaned and, at minimum, undergo high-level disinfection after each use. Meticulous cleaning is necessary before high-level disinfection or sterilization.
source_original.source_detail: Flexible bronchoscopes require cleaning and at least high-level disinfection after each use Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the bronchoscope-reprocessing construct and key A. Made the required internal-channel cleaning explicit, preserved the CDC minimum of high-level disinfection after each use, strengthened distractors around common reprocessing errors, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct infection-control requirement.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC disinfection/sterilization guidance; official NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC healthcare-equipment guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-16 with no newer conflicting bronchoscope-reprocessing standard identified
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Disinfection of Healthcare Equipment > flexible endoscopes/bronchoscopes, cleaning prerequisite, and standardized reprocessing steps
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the CDC requirement for proper cleaning followed by at least high-level disinfection after each use and explicitly includes internal-channel cleaning without adding unsupported disinfectant concentration or contact time.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because known infection status does not reduce reusable bronchoscope reprocessing to low-level surface disinfection.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because meticulous cleaning is a prerequisite to effective high-level disinfection/sterilization.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because internal channels are part of the required reprocessing pathway and must be cleaned/disinfected.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains both mandatory stages—thorough cleaning and at least high-level disinfection—without omitting the internal channels.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives address bronchoscope reprocessing and differ on level/sequence/completeness rather than unrelated facts.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — reusable device reprocessing and infection transmission prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC bronchoscope/endoscope guidance, cleaning prerequisite, internal-channel steps, all four alternatives, rationale, objective, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing, and NCSBN category alignment. A remained uniquely correct.
